item.title: At London’s Caractère, Emily Roux Carries Her Family Legacy Forward
item.description: At her Notting Hill restaurant, Roux balances inheritance and independence, shaping Caractère on her own terms.

item.title: U.S. Galleries and Art Spaces Shut Their Doors to Protest ICE
item.description: The commercial art world has rarely, if ever, acted in unison when politics has collided with money and power.

item.title: A Perugino Masterpiece Lands in New York for Sotheby’s Old Masters Week
item.description: On loan from the Galleria Nazionale dell’Umbria in Perugia, the artist's 'Man of Sorrows' (1495) will be on view through February 4 before heading to the Morgan Library, where it will be shown in dialogue with a Giovanni Bellini 'Pietà.'

item.title: The Most Noteworthy Cocktail Bars in Dallas, From Speakeasies to Rooftops
item.description: A guide to the bars pushing Dallas’ cocktail scene beyond margaritas and Ranch Water.

item.title: One Fine Show: “The Lost World, The Art of Minnie Evans” at the High
item.description: In Atlanta, the artist’s hallucinatory compositions challenge the boundaries of so-called folk art with their depth and technical complexity.

item.title: Team USA Athletes to Get First-Ever Pensions Under $100M Ross Stevens Gift
item.description: Team USA’s Milan Cortina roster will be the first to receive retirement benefits, thanks to a $100 million donation funding the Stevens Awards.

item.title: Jeff Bezos Backs Nuclear Power With $3.5M Grant From Earth Fund
item.description: The Bezos Earth Fund is funding a new effort to standardize nuclear reactor builds as electricity demand surges.

item.title: The Nordic Blueprint for Building A.I. Infrastructure at Scale
item.description: Anders Fryxell, chief sales officer at atNorth, examines how the Nordic region has emerged as a global leader in A.I.-ready digital infrastructure, at a moment when hyperscalers and enterprises alike are struggling to secure power, connectivity and sustainable capacity. Fryxell argues that the Nordics’ long-term investments in renewable energy, grid resilience and circular economy practices offer a practical blueprint for scaling A.I. without sacrificing reliability or climate goals.

item.title: Art Genève Courts Galleries With a Different Market Logic
item.description: This fair unfolds at a deliberately measured scale, offering galleries and collectors a setting defined by conversation and connection.

item.title: How Google’s A.I. Overviews Are Rewriting the Rules of Digital Commerce
item.description: Phillip Thune, CEO of Adthena, examines how Google’s A.I. Overviews are transforming the search landscape, from where ads appear to how consumers form intent. Thune argues that generative search represents a structural shift in digital commerce that compresses the funnel, challenges measurement and forces brands to rethink how visibility, authority and performance are earned in an A.I.-mediated world.
